title: Pulleys
prompt: A labelled principle teaching adaptation of pages 54 and 55 uses a supported load and interchangeable rope routing. Pull draws rope over one fixed pulley and raises the load with equal rope and load travel in the ideal case. Compare routes first supports the load externally, then rethreads the rope over a fixed upper pulley, around a load-mounted movable pulley and back to an upper anchor. Pulling twice the rope distance now raises the load once that distance with half the ideal effort. Lower pays rope out under a controlling hand. See-through shows anchors, rope route, two load-supporting strands, sheaves and moving block. Force and travel are overlays. Adding only fixed redirecting sheaves gives no ideal force advantage.
blurb: A teaching adaptation compares a fixed pulley with two strands supporting a movable load, trading rope travel for ideal effort.

identity.note: Pulleys is the real chapter heading on page 54 in both editions. A fixed single pulley changes direction without ideal force gain. Page 55 connects a fixed pulley and movable lower pulley with the rope end anchored above; two strands support the moving load and trade twice the rope travel for half ideal effort.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain as a principle comparison. Existing standingwave uses one tension pulley as an instrument fixture. Block and tackle is the named ten-supporting-strand application; chain hoist exploits unequal upper diameters rather than this two-strand rope route.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Intended mechanism compared using catalog prompts, existing figure metadata and prior source recommendations. Existing figure runtime not certified.

1998 and 2016 primary page text inspected. 1988 remains inaccessible and unverified.
Ideal inextensible rope and frictionless, massless sheaves. Total suspended weight is 100 N. Real bearings, rope bending and moving block weight increase effort.

The freestanding frame and wide load support are teaching fixtures. Compare routes lowers onto the support before a manual re-rig is represented. Rethreading may use a different working length of rope.
